proxmox-homelab-4a1: Epic: Convert LXC containers to unprivileged mode
Status: open
Priority: P2
Type: task
Created: 2025-12-14 04:31
Updated: 2025-12-14 06:02

Description:
CRITICAL SECURITY: Convert privileged LXC containers to unprivileged mode where possible.

## Background
All 12 LXC containers currently run with unprivileged=false. Unprivileged containers provide better security - container UID 0 maps to unprivileged user on host.

## Requirements for Unprivileged Docker-in-LXC
- unprivileged = true
- enable_nesting = true (required for Docker namespaces)
- enable_keyctl = true (required for kernel key operations)
- enable_fuse = false (set true only if using ZFS storage)

## CVE-2025-52881 Note
Recent containerd update broke Docker in LXC. Ensure lxc-pve >= 6.0.0-2 on Proxmox host.

## Migration Strategy
- Convert each LXC independently (child issues)
- Test thoroughly before moving to next
- Some LXCs may need to stay privileged
- Document any issues encountered

## Exceptions (May Need Privileged)
- Traefik (200): Needs ports 80/443
- Network Services (101): Tailscale needs NET_ADMIN

proxmox-homelab-tsr: Convert OpenWebUI LXC (501) to unprivileged
Status: open
Priority: P2
Type: task
Created: 2025-12-14 06:07
Updated: 2025-12-14 06:07

Description:
Convert LXC 501 (OpenWebUI) to unprivileged mode.

## Current Config
- Container ID: 501
- IP: 10.100.5.101
- Services: OpenWebUI, Ollama (with AMD GPU)

## Changes Required
```hcl
unprivileged   = true
enable_nesting = true
enable_keyctl  = true
```

## Potential Issues
- **GPU passthrough**: /dev/kfd and /dev/dri for AMD ROCm
- **AppArmor disabled**: Currently uses apparmor=unconfined

## Testing Checklist
- [ ] Container starts successfully
- [ ] Ollama starts and loads models
- [ ] GPU acceleration works (ROCm)
- [ ] OpenWebUI accessible
- [ ] Chat completions work
- [ ] Model switching works

## Notes
GPU passthrough is the main concern. May need device cgroup rules for /dev/kfd and /dev/dri in unprivileged mode.

Depends on (1):
  → proxmox-homelab-4a1: Epic: Convert LXC containers to unprivileged mode [P2]

# =============================================================================
# Docker LXC Module
# =============================================================================
# Opinionated module for deploying Docker-based applications in LXC containers.
# Uses lxc-base + filesync provider + remotedockercompose provider for a
# fully declarative deployment experience.
# =============================================================================

terraform {
  required_providers {
    proxmox = {
      source  = "bpg/proxmox"
      version = "~> 0.69"
    }
    filesync = {
      source  = "darshan-rambhia/filesync"
      version = "~> 0.3"
    }
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LXC Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "lxc" {
  source = "../lxc-base"

  name         = var.name
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network - dual-network architecture
  container_ip      = var.container_ip
  container_gateway = var.container_gateway
  lan_ip            = var.lan_ip
  lan_gateway       = var.lan_gateway

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Container type
  unprivileged = var.unprivileged
  template     = var.template

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key               = var.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Features
  enable_nesting = true
  enable_keyctl  = true
  enable_fuse    = false

  # Mount points
  mount_points = var.mount_points

  # Proxmox notes
  description = var.enable_proxmox_notes ? templatefile("${path.module}/templates/notes.md.tftpl", {
    service_name = var.service_name != "" ? var.service_name : var.name
    description  = var.service_description
    urls         = var.service_urls
    services     = var.services
    ssh_host     = split("/", var.container_ip)[0]
    custom_notes = var.custom_notes
    managed_by   = true
  }) : ""

  # Tags
  tags = concat(["docker"], var.tags)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File Sync - Using filesync provider directly
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Get list of all files in deploy directory, excluding specified patterns
locals {
  _all_deploy_files = var.deploy_dir != "" ? fileset(var.deploy_dir, "**") : []

  # Filter out files matching exclude patterns
  deploy_files = [
    for f in local._all_deploy_files : f
    if !anytrue([for pattern in var.exclude_patterns : can(regex(pattern, f))])
  ]
}

# Sync each file individually using filesync provider
resource "filesync_file" "config_files" {
  for_each = toset(local.deploy_files)

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${each.value}"
  destination = "${var.target_path}/${each.value}"
  host        = module.lxc.container_ip
  mode        = "0644"

  # SSH configuration - provider config is inherited but explicit for clarity
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [module.lxc]
}

# Set custom permissions for specific files
resource "filesync_file" "custom_permissions" {
  for_each = var.file_permissions

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${trimsuffix(trimprefix(each.key, var.target_path), "/")}"
  destination = each.key
  host        = module.lxc.container_ip
  mode        = each.value

  # SSH configuration
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [filesync_file.config_files]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Docker Compose
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Note: Docker Compose stack deployment is handled by the deploy directory
# containing docker-compose.yml. The filesync provider syncs the compose file
# to the container. Applications can manually run `docker compose up -d` via
# SSH if needed, or include it in post_sync_commands.

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer CE - Container Management UI
  # ==========================================================================
  portainer:
    image: portainer/portainer-ce:latest
    container_name: portainer
    command: -H unix:///var/run/docker.sock
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"   # Web UI
      - "8000:8000"   # Edge agent tunnel
    volumes:
      - ./portainer:/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Watchtower - Automatic Container Updates
  # ==========================================================================
  watchtower:
    image: containrrr/watchtower:latest
    container_name: watchtower
    environment:
      - WATCHTOWER_CLEANUP=true
      - WATCHTOWER_POLL_INTERVAL=86400  # Check daily
      - WATCHTOWER_INCLUDE_RESTARTING=true
      - WATCHTOWER_LABEL_ENABLE=true    # Only update containers with label
      - DOCKER_API_VERSION=1.52         # Match Docker daemon API version
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    restart: unless-stopped

Perfect! Now I have all the information needed. Let me compile my findings:

## Homelab Docker-in-LXC Configuration Report

Based on my exploration of the homelab codebase, here's a comprehensive analysis of the Docker-in-LXC configuration:

### 1. **LXC-Base Module Structure**

**File: `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/modules/lxc-base/main.tf`**

This is the foundational module that creates LXC containers with the following key sections:

- **Privileged vs Unprivileged Control** (line 142):
  ```hcl
  unprivileged = var.unprivileged
  ```
  This is a hard switch that determines whether the container runs privileged or unprivileged.

- **Feature Configuration via API** (lines 135-140):
  ```hcl
  dynamic "features" {
    for_each = var.unprivileged ? [1] : []
    content {
      nesting = var.enable_nesting
    }
  }
  ```
  Note: The API can ONLY set features on unprivileged containers. The comment explicitly states this limitation.

- **AppArmor + Feature Configuration via SSH** (lines 174-218):
  ```hcl
  resource "null_resource" "configure_container_features" {
    count = (var.enable_keyctl || var.enable_fuse || !var.unprivileged) && var.proxmox_ssh_host != "" ? 1 : 0
    # ...
    inline = [
      # For privileged containers: set AppArmor to unconfined
      var.unprivileged ? "echo 'Unprivileged container - skipping apparmor config'" : 
        "grep -q 'lxc.apparmor.profile' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'lxc.apparmor.profile: unconfined' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      
      # Configure features via pct set (nesting, keyctl, fuse)
      "pct set ${var.container_id} --features nesting=${var.enable_nesting ? 1 : 0},keyctl=${var.enable_keyctl ? 1 : 0},fuse=${var.enable_fuse ? 1 : 0}",
      
      # Restart container to apply changes
      "if pct status ${var.container_id} | grep -q running; then pct stop ${var.container_id} && sleep 2 && pct start ${var.container_id} && echo 'Container restarted'; fi",
    ]
  }
  ```

**Variables** (`/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/modules/lxc-base/variables.tf`):

- `unprivileged` (line 153-157): Default **true**, controls privilege level
- `enable_nesting` (line 159-163): Default **false**, required for Docker/Podman
- `enable_fuse` (line 165-169): Default **false**, only needed for ZFS storage
- `enable_keyctl` (line 171-175): Default **false**, required for kernel key operations

---

### 2. **Docker-LXC Module**

**File: `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/modules/docker-lxc/main.tf`**

This opinionated module wraps `lxc-base` with Docker-specific defaults:

```hcl
# Docker-LXC Module Configuration (lines 56-59)
enable_nesting = true    # Required for Docker namespaces
enable_keyctl  = true    # Required for kernel operations
enable_fuse    = false   # Not needed for standard Docker
```

**Default Settings** (`/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/modules/docker-lxc/variables.tf`):

- `unprivileged` (line 76-80): Default **false** (privileged for Docker compatibility)
- `template` (line 82-86): Default `debian-13-docker_1.0_amd64.tar.zst` (Docker pre-installed)

---

### 3. **Current Deployment Status**

**Privileged Containers (unprivileged = false):**
- Traefik (200) - Required for ports 80/443
- Network Services (101) - Tailscale requires NET_ADMIN
- Portainer (100)
- OpenWebUI (LXC-code)
- Obsidian Sync (LXC-code)
- Jellyfin (401)
- Immich (302)
- Media Management (402)
- n8n (LXC-code)
- Dashboards (201)
- AuthElia (LXC-code)
- Monitoring (LXC-code)

**Unprivileged Container (unprivileged = true):**
- **Immich Importer (303)** - Only one converted so far
  - Configuration (lines 147-149 in `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/apps/immich-importer/main.tf`):
    ```hcl
    unprivileged   = true
    enable_nesting = true
    enable_keyctl  = true
    ```

---

### 4. **CVE-2025-52881 Workaround**

**Location:** Beads issue tracker (`.beads/issues.jsonl`)

From the epic "Convert LXC containers to unprivileged mode" (`proxmox-homelab-4a1`):

```
## CVE-2025-52881 Note
Recent containerd update broke Docker in LXC. Ensure lxc-pve >= 6.0.0-2 on Proxmox host.
```

This is documented as a known issue that affects the migration to unprivileged containers. The workaround is to ensure the Proxmox LXC package is at version 6.0.0-2 or later.

---

### 5. **Feature Settings Control**

**Nesting** (Required for Docker):
- Set to `true` in docker-lxc module by default
- Allows containers to use Linux namespaces for Docker

**Keyctl** (Kernel Key Management):
- Set to `true` in docker-lxc module by default
- Required for Docker key operations and some system functions
- Can only be configured via SSH to Proxmox host (requires root@pam)

**FUSE** (Filesystem-in-Userspace):
- Set to `false` by default in both modules
- Only needed for ZFS or other advanced filesystem operations
- Can only be configured via SSH to Proxmox host (requires root@pam)

---

### 6. **Key Implementation Details**

**API Token Limitations:**
- Cannot set features on **privileged** containers (only via SSH)
- Cannot set keyctl and fuse even on unprivileged containers (only via SSH)
- Cannot modify GPU device passthrough (manually added in Proxmox)

**SSH Configuration for Proxmox Host:**
```hcl
variables "proxmox_ssh_host" (default "")
variable "proxmox_ssh_private_key_path" (default "")
```

These optional variables enable SSH provisioning to configure features that the API token cannot handle.

---

### 7. **Traefik Exception (Ports 80/443)**

**File:** `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/apps/traefik/main.tf` (lines 77-78)

```hcl
# MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
unprivileged = false
```

Traefik explicitly states the privileged requirement. The beads issue (proxmox-homelab-6gu) notes potential workarounds:
1. `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0`
2. Use high ports (8080/8443) with iptables redirect
3. CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE capability (may not work in unprivileged)

---

### Summary Table

| Aspect | Configuration | Notes |
|--------|---------------|-------|
| **Default Privileged** | Yes (`false`) | Can be overridden per container |
| **Nesting** | true in docker-lxc | Required for Docker |
| **Keyctl** | true in docker-lxc | Requires SSH provisioning |
| **FUSE** | false by default | Only for ZFS/advanced FS |
| **AppArmor Profile** | `unconfined` (privileged only) | SSH provisioning required |
| **Converted Containers** | 1 (immich-importer) | Others remain privileged |
| **CVE Status** | CVE-2025-52881 documented | Requires lxc-pve >= 6.0.0-2 |

## Background Context

### Current Architecture
- All 12 Docker-in-LXC containers run privileged (unprivileged=false)
- Only immich-importer (303) has been converted to unprivileged
- OpenTofu manages infrastructure via docker-lxc module → lxc-base module
- Proxmox limitation: privileged flag is read-only after LXC creation (requires destroy/recreate)

### Key Files
- `tofu/modules/lxc-base/main.tf` - Core LXC provisioning with features config via SSH
- `tofu/modules/docker-lxc/main.tf` - Docker-specific wrapper with nesting/keyctl enabled
- `tofu/apps/n8n/main.tf` - n8n config (line 36: unprivileged = false)
- `tofu/apps/openwebui/main.tf` - OpenWebUI config (line 58: unprivileged = false)

### Requirements for Unprivileged Docker-in-LXC
- unprivileged = true
- enable_nesting = true (already set in docker-lxc module)
- enable_keyctl = true (already set in docker-lxc module)
- enable_fuse = false (unless ZFS storage)
- CVE-2025-52881: Ensure lxc-pve >= 6.0.0-2 on Proxmox host

### N8N (502) - Low Risk Pilot
- Simple web app, no special requirements
- Uses named Docker volume (n8n_data)
- Runs as node user (UID 1000)

Create `scripts/migration/` with the following scripts:

**File: `scripts/migration/backup-docker-volumes.sh`**
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Backup Docker volumes from an LXC container
# Usage: ./backup-docker-volumes.sh <container_id> <backup_dir>

VMID="$1"
BACKUP_DIR="${2:-/tank/backups/migration}"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

# Stop Docker to ensure consistent backup
ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker compose -f /config/docker-compose.yml stop"

# Export all Docker volumes
ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume ls -q" | while read vol; do
    echo "Backing up volume: $vol"
    ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
        -v ${vol}:/source:ro \
        -v /tmp/backup:/backup \
        alpine tar czf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz -C /source ."
    ssh root@homelab "pct pull $VMID /tmp/backup/${vol}.tar.gz $BACKUP_DIR/${VMID}-${vol}.tar.gz"
done

echo "Volumes backed up to $BACKUP_DIR"
```

**File: `scripts/migration/restore-docker-volumes.sh`**
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Restore Docker volumes to an LXC container
# Usage: ./restore-docker-volumes.sh <container_id> <backup_dir>

VMID="$1"
BACKUP_DIR="${2:-/tank/backups/migration}"

for archive in $BACKUP_DIR/${VMID}-*.tar.gz; do
    vol=$(basename "$archive" | sed "s/${VMID}-//" | sed 's/.tar.gz//')
    echo "Restoring volume: $vol"
    
    # Push archive to container
    ssh root@homelab "pct push $VMID $archive /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"
    
    # Create volume and restore
    ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume create $vol"
    ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
        -v ${vol}:/dest \
        -v /tmp:/backup \
        alpine sh -c 'cd /dest && tar xzf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz'"
done
```

Create `scripts/migration/` with the following scripts:

**File: `scripts/migration/backup-docker-volumes.sh`**
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Backup Docker volumes from an LXC container
# Usage: ./backup-docker-volumes.sh <container_id> <backup_dir>

VMID="$1"
BACKUP_DIR="${2:-/tank/backups/migration}"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

# Stop Docker to ensure consistent backup
ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker compose -f /config/docker-compose.yml stop"

# Export all Docker volumes
ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume ls -q" | while read vol; do
    echo "Backing up volume: $vol"
    ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
        -v ${vol}:/source:ro \
        -v /tmp/backup:/backup \
        alpine tar czf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz -C /source ."
    ssh root@homelab "pct pull $VMID /tmp/backup/${vol}.tar.gz $BACKUP_DIR/${VMID}-${vol}.tar.gz"
done

echo "Volumes backed up to $BACKUP_DIR"
```

**File: `scripts/migration/restore-docker-volumes.sh`**
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Restore Docker volumes to an LXC container
# Usage: ./restore-docker-volumes.sh <container_id> <backup_dir>

VMID="$1"
BACKUP_DIR="${2:-/tank/backups/migration}"

for archive in $BACKUP_DIR/${VMID}-*.tar.gz; do
    vol=$(basename "$archive" | sed "s/${VMID}-//" | sed 's/.tar.gz//')
    echo "Restoring volume: $vol"
    
    # Push archive to container
    ssh root@homelab "pct push $VMID $archive /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"
    
    # Create volume and restore
    ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume create $vol"
    ssh root@homelab "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
        -v ${vol}:/dest \
        -v /tmp:/backup \
        alpine sh -c 'cd /dest && tar xzf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz'"
done
```

---

**Container**: 502 | **IP**: 10.100.5.102 | **Risk**: Low (simple web app)

```bash

./scripts/migration/backup-docker-volumes.sh 502
```

### Step 2.2: Update Configuration

**File**: `tofu/apps/n8n/main.tf` (line 36)
```hcl
unprivileged = true  # Changed from false
```

**File**: `tofu/apps/n8n/deploy/docker-compose.yml`
- Replace `portainer-agent` with `portainer-edge-agent`

variable "enable_gpu" {

}

```hcl
module "lxc" {
  # ... existing ...

}

```hcl
unprivileged = true   # Changed from false

# Plan: Unprivileged Docker-in-LXC Migration with Edge Agents

## Overview

Convert privileged Docker-in-LXC containers to unprivileged mode for improved security, using n8n and OpenWebUI as pilot containers. Simultaneously migrate from standard Portainer Agents (port 9001) to Edge Agents (outbound to port 8000).

**Key Constraint**: Proxmox's `privileged` flag is immutable after LXC creation - requires destroy/recreate workflow.

---

```

### 1.2 Create Migration Scripts
Create `scripts/migration/` directory with:
- `backup-docker-volumes.sh` - Export Docker volumes via tar
- `restore-docker-volumes.sh` - Import Docker volumes after recreation

### 1.3 Prepare Edge Agent Infrastructure
- Enable Edge Compute in Portainer Settings (port 8000 already configured)
- Create 1Password items for Edge credentials per container

---

## Phase 2: n8n Migration (Low Risk Pilot)

**Container**: 502 | **IP**: 10.100.5.102 | **Risk**: Low (simple web app)

### Step 2.1: Backup
```bash
task backup:now APP=n8n
./scripts/migration/backup-docker-volumes.sh 502
```

### Step 2.2: Update Configuration

**File**: `tofu/apps/n8n/main.tf` (line 36)
```hcl
unprivileged = true  # Changed from false
```

**File**: `tofu/apps/n8n/deploy/docker-compose.yml`
- Replace `portainer-agent` with `portainer-edge-agent`
- Remove port 9001 exposure
- Add EDGE_ID/EDGE_KEY environment variables

### Step 2.3: Recreate Container
```bash
# Remove from state
tofu state rm 'module.n8n.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc'

# Destroy old privileged container
ssh root@homelab "pct stop 502 && pct destroy 502"

# Create new unprivileged container
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# Restore data
./scripts/migration/restore-docker-volumes.sh 502
```

### Step 2.4: Verify
- [ ] Container starts, Docker daemon running
- [ ] n8n UI accessible at https://n8n.homelab.rambtech.dev
- [ ] Workflows load and execute
- [ ] Edge Agent connected in Portainer

---

## Phase 3: OpenWebUI Migration (High Risk Pilot)

**Container**: 501 | **IP**: 10.100.5.101 | **Risk**: High (GPU passthrough)

### Step 3.1: Backup
```bash
task backup:now APP=openwebui
./scripts/migration/backup-docker-volumes.sh 501
# Backup 32GB Ollama models separately
ssh root@homelab "pct exec 501 -- tar czf /tmp/ollama-models.tar.gz /root/.ollama"
```

### Step 3.2: Update Module for GPU Support

**File**: `tofu/modules/docker-lxc/variables.tf`
```hcl
variable "enable_gpu" {
  description = "Enable AMD GPU passthrough"
  type        = bool
  default     = false
}
```

**File**: `tofu/modules/docker-lxc/main.tf`
```hcl
module "lxc" {
  # ... existing ...
  enable_gpu = var.enable_gpu
}
```

### Step 3.3: Update OpenWebUI Configuration

**File**: `tofu/apps/openwebui/main.tf` (line 58)
```hcl
unprivileged = true   # Changed from false
enable_gpu   = true   # Add this line
```

**File**: `tofu/apps/openwebui/deploy/docker-compose.yml`
- Replace `portainer-agent` with `portainer-edge-agent`
- **Try removing** `security_opt: apparmor=unconfined` (LXC handles this)
- Restrict `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` (security fix)
- Set `ENABLE_SIGNUP=false` (security fix)

### Step 3.4: Recreate Container
```bash
tofu state rm 'module.openwebui.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc'
ssh root@homelab "pct stop 501 && pct destroy 501"
task tofu:apply APP=openwebui
./scripts/migration/restore-docker-volumes.sh 501

ssh root@homelab "pct push 501 /tank/backups/migration/501-ollama-models.tar.gz /tmp/ && pct exec 501 -- tar xzf /tmp/ollama-models.tar.gz -C /"
```

### Step 3.5: Verify
- [ ] Container starts, Docker daemon running
- [ ] GPU accessible: `pct exec 501 -- ls -la /dev/dri /dev/kfd`
- [ ] Ollama GPU works: `docker exec ollama rocminfo`
- [ ] OpenWebUI chat completions work
- [ ] Edge Agent connected in Portainer

1. Add back `apparmor=unconfined` to docker-compose
2. Or add cgroup rules to `/etc/pve/lxc/501.conf`

---

## Phase 4: Rollout to Remaining Containers

After successful pilots, proceed in order:

| Priority | Container | ID | Notes |
|----------|-----------|-----|-------|
| 1 | Dashboards | 201 | Low risk |
| 1 | Authelia | 202 | Low risk |
| 1 | Obsidian Sync | 503 | Low risk |
| 1 | Monitoring | 500 | Low risk |
| 2 | Immich | 304 | GPU passthrough |
| 2 | Jellyfin | 401 | GPU transcoding |
| 2 | Portainer | 100 | Management plane |
| 3 | Network Services | 101 | May stay privileged (Tailscale) |
| 3 | Media Management | 402 | May stay privileged (VPN TUN) |
| 3 | Traefik | 200 | May stay privileged (ports 80/443) |

---

## Files to Modify

### Migration Scripts (New)
- `scripts/migration/backup-docker-volumes.sh`
- `scripts/migration/restore-docker-volumes.sh`

### Module Updates
- `tofu/modules/docker-lxc/variables.tf` - Add `enable_gpu` variable
- `tofu/modules/docker-lxc/main.tf` - Pass `enable_gpu` to lxc-base

### n8n Updates
- `tofu/apps/n8n/main.tf` - Set `unprivileged = true`
- `tofu/apps/n8n/deploy/docker-compose.yml` - Edge Agent config

### OpenWebUI Updates
- `tofu/apps/openwebui/main.tf` - Set `unprivileged = true`, `enable_gpu = true`
- `tofu/apps/openwebui/deploy/docker-compose.yml` - Edge Agent, security fixes

---

## Rollback Plan

For any failed migration:
```bash
# Restore from vzdump backup
task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-<id>-<timestamp>.tar.zst TARGET_ID=<id>

# Revert git changes
git checkout tofu/apps/<app>/main.tf
git checkout tofu/apps/<app>/deploy/docker-compose.yml

# Re-import to state
tofu import 'module.<app>.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc' 'pve/lxc/<id>'
```

---

- `proxmox-homelab-z80` - Remove Portainer Agent port 9001 exposure

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Backup Docker Volumes from LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# Usage: ./backup-docker-volumes.sh <container_id> [backup_dir]
#
# Exports all Docker volumes from an LXC container to tar.gz archives.
# Stops Docker compose stack to ensure consistent backup.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

VMID="${1:-}"
BACKUP_DIR="${2:-/tank/backups/migration}"
PROXMOX_HOST="${PROXMOX_HOST:-homelab}"

if [[ -z "$VMID" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <container_id> [backup_dir]"
    echo "Example: $0 502 /tank/backups/migration"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== Backing up Docker volumes from LXC $VMID ==="
echo "Backup directory: $BACKUP_DIR"

# Create backup directory on Proxmox host
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "mkdir -p ${BACKUP_DIR}"

# Stop Docker compose stack for consistent backup
echo "Stopping Docker services..."
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- bash -c 'cd /config && docker compose stop'" || true

# Get list of Docker volumes
echo "Getting list of Docker volumes..."
VOLUMES=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume ls -q" || echo "")

if [[ -z "$VOLUMES" ]]; then
    echo "No Docker volumes found in container $VMID"
else
    echo "Found volumes: $VOLUMES"

    # Backup each volume
    for vol in $VOLUMES; do
        echo "Backing up volume: $vol"

        # Create backup inside container using alpine
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
            -v ${vol}:/source:ro \
            -v /tmp/backup:/backup \
            alpine tar czf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz -C /source ."

        # Copy backup from container to Proxmox host backup dir
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct pull $VMID /tmp/backup/${vol}.tar.gz ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-${vol}.tar.gz"

        # Clean up temp file in container
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/backup/${vol}.tar.gz"

        echo "  -> Saved to ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-${vol}.tar.gz"
    done
fi

# Also backup the /config directory (compose files, app data)
echo "Backing up /config directory..."
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- tar czf /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz -C / config" || true
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct pull $VMID /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-config.tar.gz" || true
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz" || true

# Restart Docker compose stack
echo "Restarting Docker services..."
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- bash -c 'cd /config && docker compose up -d'" || true

echo ""
echo "=== Backup complete ==="
echo "Backup files:"
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "ls -lh ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-*" 2>/dev/null || echo "No backup files found"

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Restore Docker Volumes to LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# Usage: ./restore-docker-volumes.sh <container_id> [backup_dir]
#
# Restores Docker volumes from tar.gz archives to an LXC container.
# Should be run after container recreation.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

VMID="${1:-}"
BACKUP_DIR="${2:-/tank/backups/migration}"
PROXMOX_HOST="${PROXMOX_HOST:-homelab}"

if [[ -z "$VMID" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <container_id> [backup_dir]"
    echo "Example: $0 502 /tank/backups/migration"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== Restoring Docker volumes to LXC $VMID ==="
echo "Backup directory: $BACKUP_DIR"

# Check container is running
if ! ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct status $VMID" | grep -q running; then
    echo "Starting container $VMID..."
    ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct start $VMID"
    sleep 10  # Wait for container to fully boot
fi

# Wait for Docker to be ready
echo "Waiting for Docker daemon..."
for i in {1..30}; do
    if ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker info" &>/dev/null; then
        echo "Docker is ready"
        break
    fi
    sleep 2
done

# Restore /config directory first (contains docker-compose.yml)
CONFIG_BACKUP="${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-config.tar.gz"
if ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "test -f ${CONFIG_BACKUP}"; then
    echo "Restoring /config directory..."
    ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct push $VMID ${CONFIG_BACKUP} /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz"
    ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- tar xzf /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz -C /"
    ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz"
    echo "  -> Restored /config"
else
    echo "No config backup found at ${CONFIG_BACKUP}"
fi

# Get list of volume backups
echo "Looking for volume backups..."
VOLUME_BACKUPS=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "ls ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | grep -v config.tar.gz" || echo "")

if [[ -z "$VOLUME_BACKUPS" ]]; then
    echo "No volume backups found for container $VMID"
else
    for archive in $VOLUME_BACKUPS; do
        # Extract volume name from filename (VMID-volumename.tar.gz)
        filename=$(basename "$archive")
        vol=$(echo "$filename" | sed "s/${VMID}-//" | sed 's/.tar.gz//')

        echo "Restoring volume: $vol"

        # Push archive to container
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct push $VMID ${archive} /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"

        # Create volume if it doesn't exist
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume create $vol" 2>/dev/null || true

        # Restore volume contents using alpine
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
            -v ${vol}:/dest \
            -v /tmp:/backup \
            alpine sh -c 'cd /dest && tar xzf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz'"

        # Clean up temp file
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"

        echo "  -> Restored volume: $vol"
    done
fi

# Start Docker compose stack
echo "Starting Docker services..."
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- bash -c 'cd /config && docker compose up -d'" || true

echo ""
echo "=== Restore complete ==="
echo "Docker containers:"
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker ps"

# =============================================================================
# Docker LXC Module
# =============================================================================
# Opinionated module for deploying Docker-based applications in LXC containers.
# Uses lxc-base + filesync provider + remotedockercompose provider for a
# fully declarative deployment experience.
# =============================================================================

terraform {
  required_providers {
    proxmox = {
      source  = "bpg/proxmox"
      version = "~> 0.69"
    }
    filesync = {
      source  = "darshan-rambhia/filesync"
      version = "~> 0.3"
    }
  }
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LXC Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "lxc" {
  source = "../lxc-base"

  name         = var.name
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network - dual-network architecture
  container_ip      = var.container_ip
  container_gateway = var.container_gateway
  lan_ip            = var.lan_ip
  lan_gateway       = var.lan_gateway

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Container type
  unprivileged = var.unprivileged
  template     = var.template

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key               = var.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Features
  enable_nesting = true
  enable_keyctl  = true
  enable_fuse    = false

  # Mount points
  mount_points = var.mount_points

  # Proxmox notes
  description = var.enable_proxmox_notes ? templatefile("${path.module}/templates/notes.md.tftpl", {
    service_name = var.service_name != "" ? var.service_name : var.name
    description  = var.service_description
    urls         = var.service_urls
    services     = var.services
    ssh_host     = split("/", var.container_ip)[0]
    custom_notes = var.custom_notes
    managed_by   = true
  }) : ""

  # Tags
  tags = concat(["docker"], var.tags)
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# File Sync - Using filesync provider directly
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Get list of all files in deploy directory, excluding specified patterns
locals {
  _all_deploy_files = var.deploy_dir != "" ? fileset(var.deploy_dir, "**") : []

  # Filter out files matching exclude patterns
  deploy_files = [
    for f in local._all_deploy_files : f
    if !anytrue([for pattern in var.exclude_patterns : can(regex(pattern, f))])
  ]
}

# Sync each file individually using filesync provider
resource "filesync_file" "config_files" {
  for_each = toset(local.deploy_files)

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${each.value}"
  destination = "${var.target_path}/${each.value}"
  host        = module.lxc.container_ip
  mode        = "0644"

  # SSH configuration - provider config is inherited but explicit for clarity
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [module.lxc]
}

# Set custom permissions for specific files
resource "filesync_file" "custom_permissions" {
  for_each = var.file_permissions

  source      = "${var.deploy_dir}/${trimsuffix(trimprefix(each.key, var.target_path), "/")}"
  destination = each.key
  host        = module.lxc.container_ip
  mode        = each.value

  # SSH configuration
  ssh_user     = "root"
  ssh_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  depends_on = [filesync_file.config_files]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Docker Compose
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Note: Docker Compose stack deployment is handled by the deploy directory
# containing docker-compose.yml. The filesync provider syncs the compose file
# to the container. Applications can manually run `docker compose up -d` via
# SSH if needed, or include it in post_sync_commands.

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenWebUI - AI Chat Interface
  # ==========================================================================
  openwebui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    container_name: openwebui
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434
      - WEBUI_AUTH=true
      - WEBUI_NAME=Homelab AI
      - ENABLE_SIGNUP=true
      - DEFAULT_MODELS=llama3.2:latest
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./openwebui:/app/backend/data
    depends_on:
      - ollama
    # Required for Docker in LXC
    security_opt:
      - apparmor=unconfined
    # DNS settings for external resolution
    dns:
      - 8.8.8.8
      - 1.1.1.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Ollama - Local LLM Backend
  # ==========================================================================
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:rocm
    container_name: ollama
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*
      - HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      # Reuse existing Ollama data (32GB of models) from native install
      - /root/.ollama:/root/.ollama
    # AMD GPU passthrough via ROCM
    devices:
      - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    # Required for Docker in LXC
    security_opt:
      - apparmor=unconfined
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Agent
  # ==========================================================================
  portainer-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    container_name: portainer-agent
    ports:
      - "9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
    # Required for Docker in LXC
    security_opt:
      - apparmor=unconfined
    restart: unless-stopped

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenWebUI - AI Chat Interface
  # ==========================================================================
  openwebui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    container_name: openwebui
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434
      - WEBUI_AUTH=true
      - WEBUI_NAME=Homelab AI
      - ENABLE_SIGNUP=true
      - DEFAULT_MODELS=llama3.2:latest
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./openwebui:/app/backend/data
    depends_on:
      - ollama
    # Required for Docker in LXC
    security_opt:
      - apparmor=unconfined
    # DNS settings for external resolution
    dns:
      - 8.8.8.8
      - 1.1.1.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Ollama - Local LLM Backend
  # ==========================================================================
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:rocm
    container_name: ollama
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*
      - HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      # Reuse existing Ollama data (32GB of models) from native install
      - /root/.ollama:/root/.ollama
    # AMD GPU passthrough via ROCM
    devices:
      - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    # Required for Docker in LXC
    security_opt:
      - apparmor=unconfined
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Agent
  # ==========================================================================
  portainer-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    container_name: portainer-agent
    ports:
      - "9001:9001"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
    # Required for Docker in LXC
    security_opt:
      - apparmor=unconfined
    restart: unless-stopped

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenWebUI - AI Chat Interface
  # ==========================================================================
  openwebui:
    image: ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
    container_name: openwebui
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://ollama:11434
      - WEBUI_AUTH=true
      - WEBUI_NAME=Homelab AI
      - ENABLE_SIGNUP=false  # Security: Disable public signup
      - DEFAULT_MODELS=llama3.2:latest
    ports:
      - "3000:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./openwebui:/app/backend/data
    depends_on:
      - ollama
    # DNS settings for external resolution
    dns:
      - 8.8.8.8
      - 1.1.1.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Ollama - Local LLM Backend (AMD GPU Accelerated)
  # ==========================================================================
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:rocm
    container_name: ollama
    environment:
      - OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0
      - OLLAMA_ORIGINS=http://localhost,http://openwebui,https://ai.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      # Reuse existing Ollama data (32GB of models) from native install
      - /root/.ollama:/root/.ollama
    # AMD GPU passthrough via ROCM
    devices:
      - /dev/kfd:/dev/kfd
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri
    group_add:
      - video
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Secure container management
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-openwebui
  portainer-edge-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 0
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  portainer_agent_data:

# OpenTofu IaC Commands
# https://taskfile.dev
#
# Each app has its own state file in tofu/apps/<app>/
# Use APP=dashboards|openwebui|portainer|etc to specify which app

version: '3'

vars:
  TOFU_DIR: "tofu"

tasks:
  tofu:init:
    desc: "Initialize OpenTofu for an app (APP=dashboards|openwebui|portainer)"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu init
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:plan:
    desc: "Plan infrastructure changes for an app"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - pwd
      - tofu plan -out=tfplan
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    preconditions:
      - sh: test -d .terraform
        msg: "Run 'task tofu:init APP={{.APP}}' first"

  tofu:apply:
    desc: "Apply planned infrastructure changes for an app (optional: REPLACE='resource.name')"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu apply {{if .REPLACE}}-replace='{{.REPLACE}}' -auto-approve{{else}}tfplan{{end}}
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    preconditions:
      - sh: '{{if .REPLACE}}true{{else}}test -f tfplan{{end}}'
        msg: "Run 'task tofu:plan APP={{.APP}}' first"

  tofu:destroy:
    desc: "Destroy an app's infrastructure"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - echo "⚠️  This will destroy {{.APP}} infrastructure!"
      - tofu destroy
    requires:

content.text: The API token doesn't have permission to configure device passthrough (GPU). The lxc-base module handles features via SSH, but the initial container creation with GPU passthrough still fails. Let me check how GPU is configured in lxc-base:

I see the issue. The `device_passthrough` blocks are in the LXC resource itself, which requires root@pam permissions. However, the module already has SSH-based configuration via `null_resource.configure_container_features`. I need to:

1. Remove GPU passthrough from the Proxmox API call (create LXC without GPU)
2. Add GPU devices via SSH to Proxmox (similar to how features are configured)

Let me modify the lxc-base module to add GPU devices via SSH instead of via the API:

content.text: Now let me add a new null_resource for GPU configuration after the existing one:

input.new_string:
# Configure GPU passthrough via SSH to Proxmox host
# The API token cannot set device_passthrough - requires root@pam
# This adds /dev/dri/card0, /dev/dri/renderD128, and /dev/kfd for AMD GPU
resource "null_resource" "configure_gpu_passthrough" {
  count = var.enable_gpu && var.proxmox_ssh_host != "" ? 1 : 0

  depends_on = [
    proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc,
    null_resource.configure_container_features
  ]

  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
    enable_gpu   = var.enable_gpu
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    connection {
      type        = "ssh"
      host        = var.proxmox_ssh_host
      user        = "root"
      private_key = file(var.proxmox_ssh_private_key_path)
    }

    inline = [
      # Stop container before adding devices
      "if pct status ${var.container_id} | grep -q running; then pct stop ${var.container_id}; sleep 2; fi",

      # Add GPU devices via direct config modification
      # Using pct set --dev0/1/2 doesn't work for /dev/dri, so we modify conf directly
      "grep -q 'dev0:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'dev0: /dev/dri/card0,gid=44' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      "grep -q 'dev1:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'dev1: /dev/dri/renderD128,gid=104' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      "grep -q 'dev2:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'dev2: /dev/kfd' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",

      # Add cgroup permissions for GPU (required for unprivileged containers)
      "grep -q 'lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 226:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 226:* rwm' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      "grep -q 'lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 234:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 234:* rwm' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",

      # Start container
      "pct start ${var.container_id}",

      # Wait for container to get IP
      "echo 'Waiting for container to get IP...'",
      "for i in $(seq 1 15); do IP=$(pct exec ${var.container_id} -- ip -4 addr show eth0 2>/dev/null | grep inet | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d/ -f1); if [ -n \"$IP\" ] && [ \"$IP\" != \"pending\" ]; then echo \"Got IP: $IP\"; break; fi; sleep 2; done",

      "echo 'GPU passthrough configured for container ${var.container_id}'"
    ]
  }
}

# Wait for container to get DHCP IP
resource "time_sleep" "wait_for_ip" {
  depends_on = [
    proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc,
    null_resource.configure_container_features,
    null_resource.configure_gpu_passthrough
  ]
  create_duration = "15s"
}

# Traefik - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/

name: traefik

services:
  traefik:
    container_name: traefik
    image: traefik:v3.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"        # HTTP
      - "443:443"      # HTTPS
      - "8082:8082"    # Metrics
    environment:
      - CF_DNS_API_TOKEN=${CF_DNS_API_TOKEN}
      - CF_API_EMAIL=${CF_API_EMAIL}
    volumes:
      # Static config (synced by docker-host module to /config/static/)
      - /config/static/traefik.yml:/etc/traefik/traefik.yml:ro
      # Dynamic configs (synced by docker-host module to /config/dynamic/)
      - /config/dynamic:/config/dynamic:ro
      # Certificates (Docker volume for persistence across restarts)
      - certs:/config/certs
      # Logs (Docker volume)
      - logs:/config/logs
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "traefik", "healthcheck", "--ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # Portainer Agent for remote management
  portainer-agent:
    container_name: portainer_agent
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    ports:
      - 9001:9001
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  certs:
  logs:

# Traefik - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/

name: traefik

services:
  traefik:
    container_name: traefik
    image: traefik:v3.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"        # HTTP
      - "443:443"      # HTTPS
      - "8082:8082"    # Metrics
    environment:
      - CF_DNS_API_TOKEN=${CF_DNS_API_TOKEN}
      - CF_API_EMAIL=${CF_API_EMAIL}
    volumes:
      # Static config (synced by docker-host module to /config/static/)
      - /config/static/traefik.yml:/etc/traefik/traefik.yml:ro
      # Dynamic configs (synced by docker-host module to /config/dynamic/)
      - /config/dynamic:/config/dynamic:ro
      # Certificates (Docker volume for persistence across restarts)
      - certs:/config/certs
      # Logs (Docker volume)
      - logs:/config/logs
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "traefik", "healthcheck", "--ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # Portainer Agent for remote management
  portainer-agent:
    container_name: portainer_agent
    image: portainer/agent:latest
    ports:
      - 9001:9001
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  certs:
  logs:

I see - the Portainer route is managed by the `traefik-route` module in the `portainer` app. That module generates the dynamic config and syncs it to Traefik. The TCP tunnel route needs to be added to the traefik-route module or separately.

Let me check the traefik-route module to see if it supports TCP routes:

     2→# Traefik Route Module
     3→# =============================================================================
     4→# Generates and syncs Traefik dynamic configuration for an app.
     5→# Each app can self-register its routes without modifying Traefik configs.
     6→#
     7→# Features:

    12→#

    33→    filesync = {

    50→    entryPoints = var.internal_entrypoint
    51→    service     = var.app_name
    52→    tls = {
    53→      certResolver = var.cert_resolver
    54→    }
    55→    middlewares = var.internal_middlewares
    56→  } : null
    57→
    58→  # Public route (web HTTP - Cloudflare Flexible SSL forwards HTTP to origin)
    59→  public_route = var.public_domain != "" ? {
    60→    rule        = "Host(`${var.public_domain}`)"
    61→    entryPoints = var.public_entrypoint
    62→    service     = var.app_name
    63→    middlewares = var.public_middlewares
    64→  } : null
    65→
    66→  # Service configuration

    72→        ]
    73→      },

    75→    )
    76→  }
    77→

    81→      routers = merge(
    82→        local.internal_route != null ? { "${var.app_name}" = local.internal_route } : {},
    83→        local.public_route != null ? { "${var.app_name}-public" = local.public_route } : {}

content.text:
That's a good question. Looking at the current Traefik docker-compose, there's a Portainer **Agent** (not Edge Agent) in Traefik:

```yaml
# Portainer Agent for remote management
portainer-agent:
  container_name: portainer_agent
  image: portainer/agent:latest
  ports:
    - 9001:9001
```

This is a regular Portainer Agent that exposes port 9001 directly - it doesn't go through Traefik. It's there so Portainer can manage the Traefik container's Docker environment.

The **Edge Agent** (which we're setting up for n8n and OpenWebUI) is different - it makes an **outbound** connection to Portainer's tunnel on port 8000. The Edge Agents are connecting to `portainer.homelab.rambtech.dev:8000` which resolves to Traefik's LAN IP (192.168.1.235).

Since Traefik is the ingress point for all `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` traffic, we need Traefik to forward port 8000 traffic to Portainer. Alternatively, we could:

1. **Direct connection** - Have Edge Agents connect directly to Portainer's IP:8000 (`10.100.1.100:8000`)
2. **Through Traefik** - Route port 8000 via Traefik (what we're doing)

Option 1 is simpler but requires the Edge Agent environment to use a different hostname. The EDGE_KEY encodes the tunnel URL, so we'd need to regenerate the Edge credentials with the direct IP.

Which approach would you prefer?

Looking at the Traefik docker-compose again:

```yaml
# Portainer Agent for remote management
portainer-agent:
  container_name: portainer_agent
  image: portainer/agent:latest
  ports:
    - 9001:9001
```

This is a **regular Portainer Agent** running alongside Traefik - it's not going through Traefik. It exposes port 9001 directly on the Traefik LXC so Portainer can manage Traefik's Docker environment.

The issue is with the **Edge Agents** on n8n and OpenWebUI. They're trying to connect to `portainer.homelab.rambtech.dev:8000` which resolves to Traefik's IP (192.168.1.235), but Traefik doesn't listen on port 8000.

**Simpler solution**: The Edge Agents should connect directly to Portainer at `10.100.1.100:8000` instead of going through Traefik. This requires regenerating the Edge credentials in Portainer with the direct IP/hostname.

Would you like to:
1. **Regenerate Edge credentials** in Portainer using direct IP `10.100.1.100:8000` (simpler, no Traefik changes needed)
2. **Route through Traefik** by adding port 8000 TCP passthrough (what I was doing)

Option 1 is cleaner - Edge Agents don't need to go through the reverse proxy since they're internal-only connections.
ofcourse they shouldnt go through traefik

User requested security hardening for their homelab by:

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- Unprivileged LXC containers with Docker (nesting=1, keyctl=1, fuse=0)
- Portainer Edge Agents vs standard Portainer Agents (outbound vs inbound connections)
- GPU passthrough in unprivileged LXC (AMD Radeon - /dev/kfd, /dev/dri)

- CVE-2025-52881 workaround (requires lxc-pve >= 6.0.0-2)

```hcl
# GPU Device Passthrough and custom devices are configured via SSH
# The API token doesn't have permission for device_passthrough (requires root@pam)
# See null_resource.configure_gpu_passthrough below

# Configure GPU passthrough via SSH to Proxmox host
resource "null_resource" "configure_gpu_passthrough" {
  count = var.enable_gpu && var.proxmox_ssh_host != "" ? 1 : 0

  depends_on = [
    proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc,
    null_resource.configure_container_features
  ]

  triggers = {
    container_id = var.container_id
    enable_gpu   = var.enable_gpu
  }

  provisioner "remote-exec" {
    connection {
      type        = "ssh"
      host        = var.proxmox_ssh_host
      user        = "root"
      private_key = file(var.proxmox_ssh_private_key_path)
    }

    inline = [
      "if pct status ${var.container_id} | grep -q running; then pct stop ${var.container_id}; sleep 2; fi",
      "grep -q 'dev0:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'dev0: /dev/dri/card0,gid=44' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      "grep -q 'dev1:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'dev1: /dev/dri/renderD128,gid=104' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      "grep -q 'dev2:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'dev2: /dev/kfd' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      "grep -q 'lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 226:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 226:* rwm' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      "grep -q 'lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 234:' /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf || echo 'lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow: c 234:* rwm' >> /etc/pve/lxc/${var.container_id}.conf",
      "pct start ${var.container_id}",
      "echo 'Waiting for container to get IP...'",
      "for i in $(seq 1 15); do IP=$(pct exec ${var.container_id} -- ip -4 addr show eth0 2>/dev/null | grep inet | awk '{print $2}' | cut -d/ -f1); if [ -n \"$IP\" ] && [ \"$IP\" != \"pending\" ]; then echo \"Got IP: $IP\"; break; fi; sleep 2; done",
      "echo 'GPU passthrough configured for container ${var.container_id}'"
    ]
  }
}

Here are the search results for troubleshooting Portainer Edge Agent "short poll request failed" errors:

## Common Causes and Solutions

### 1. Check EDGE_ID and EDGE_KEY Configuration
First, check your EDGE_ID and your EDGE_KEY. In most cases, these are incorrectly set and prevent proper communication between the Edge Agent and the Portainer instance.

### 2. Firewall and Port Configuration
Portainer now requires that only the 9443 and 8000 TCP ports are exposed.(no content)Port 8000 is a TLS tunnel server used to create a secure tunnel between the agent and the Portainer instance.(no content)If that doesn't help, check your firewall. Both port 8000 of the Portainer instance needs to be accessible.

### 3. Self-Signed Certificate Issues
If your Portainer instance is deployed with TLS, the agent will use HTTPS for the connection it makes back to Portainer. However, if your Portainer instance uses a self-signed certificate, the Edge Agent must be deployed with the `-e EDGE_INSECURE_POLL=1` flag. If you do not deploy the Edge Agent with this flag, the agent won't be able to communicate with the Portainer instance.

### 4. Timeout Issues (High Latency Environments)
After troubleshooting, I found that the default request timeout of 10 seconds is not sufficient for high latency environment. The timeout is set to 10 seconds and cannot be changed from outside.

### 5. Context Deadline Exceeded
Some users have reported errors like "context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)" which indicates network connectivity or timeout issues between the agent and the Portainer server.

### 6. Decode and Verify Your EDGE_KEY
You can decode your EDGE_KEY using any online base64 decoder like base64code.com. Check if the protocol (http or https) mismatches what you used to configure your main Portainer instance.

### 7. DNS Resolution
On the host that is running the Portainer Edge Agent, check if the hostname resolves correctly. This should show you at least the IPv4 address of the Portainer instance.

### 8. Testing Connectivity
You can test port 8000 connectivity using netcat:
```bash
echo -e "\n" | nc portainer.mydomain.com 8000
```
In case you don't see any response, check your firewall and check if you've exposed port 8000 on the Portainer container.

### 9. Domain-Related Issues
When using a four level URL as portainer URL for edge agent endpoint creation, the resulted KEY cannot be decoded and the edge agent cannot connect to portainer server.

### Debugging Steps Summary:
1. Verify EDGE_ID and EDGE_KEY are correct
2. Ensure ports 9443 and 8000 are accessible through firewalls
3. Add `EDGE_INSECURE_POLL=1` if using self-signed certificates
4. Decode and verify the EDGE_KEY contains correct URLs and protocol
5. Test DNS resolution from the Edge Agent host
6. Test direct connectivity to port 8000

content.content:
# Portainer Edge Agent Polling Explained

## How Polling Works

"Agents poll the Portainer instance every 5 seconds by default (this is defined in Portainer settings)." During each poll, the agent checks if Portainer needs it for interactive management.

## Portainer Server URL Purpose

The join token contains the Portainer instance API URL, which tells the Edge Agent where to connect—essentially how the agent "calls home" to Portainer.

## Ports Used

- **Port 9443**: Serves the UI and API
- **Port 8000**: Functions as a TLS tunnel server, creating secure communication between agent and Portainer after the agent is requested

## Port 8000 vs Port 9000

Port 9000 was the original port for UI and API service. Portainer evolved to use port 9443 instead, while port 8000 was specifically added as a dedicated tunnel server for agent-to-instance communication, separating polling and tunnel establishment concerns.

- **Port 8000**: Functions as a TLS tunnel server, creating secure communication between agent and Portainer after the agent is requested

## Port 8000 vs Port 9000

Port 9000 was the original port for UI and API service. Portainer evolved to use port 9443 instead, while port 8000 was specifically added as a dedicated tunnel server for agent-to-instance communication, separating polling and tunnel establishment concerns.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the Portainer Edge Key format and structure:

## Portainer Edge Key Format

The Edge key is a base64-encoded string with the following format when decoded:
```
<portainer_instance_url>|<tunnel_server_addr>|<tunnel_server_fingerprint>|<endpoint_id>
```

### Components

The join token (EDGE_KEY) is made up of the following base64 encoded data separated by the pipe (`|`) character:

1. **The Portainer instance API URL** - This is how the Edge Agent knows how to 'call home' to your Portainer instance.

2. **The Portainer instance reverse tunnel server address** - This is identical to the API URL (unless changed during deployment or in Edge Compute settings) but with the tunnel server port (8000 is the default).

3. **The Portainer instance reverse-tunnel server fingerprint** - Prevents MITM when creating a tunnel.

4. **The environment identifier key** (endpoint / environment ID)

### Example

A decoded example looks like:
```
https://portainer.yourdomain.com|portainer.yourdomain.com:8000|aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff:00:00:00:01:00:00:00:00:00:00|3
```

### Key Details

- The tunnel server address is the default address and port of your Portainer Server instance's tunnel server. In most cases, this will be the same address as the Portainer API server URL, but without the protocol and on port 8000.

- The key can be global (endpoint ID = 0) or specific to an environment.

- Portainer requires that only the 9443 and 8000 TCP ports are exposed. Port 8000 is a TLS tunnel server used to create a secure tunnel between the agent and the Portainer instance.

### API Function

The Portainer API includes a `GenerateEdgeKey(url, host string, endpointIdentifier int) string` function in the ReverseTunnelService interface for generating these edge keys.

content.text:
The main reason the backup restoration failed for OpenWebUI was **insufficient space in `/tmp`**.

The Ollama models backup was **31GB** (the `.ollama` directory with all the AI models), and when trying to restore it, the `/tmp` directory on the container filled to 100%:

```
tar: /tmp/501-ollama-models.tar.gz: Wrote only 4096 of 10240 bytes
tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now
```

The `/tmp` directory in the LXC container didn't have enough space to hold the compressed archive during the restore process.

**Resolution**: Instead of restoring the 31GB of models, we decided to pull fresh models. We pulled `llama3.2:1b` (a smaller model) to verify Ollama + GPU was working correctly. The larger models (like `llama3.2:3b`, `deepseek-coder`, etc. that were in the original backup) would need to be pulled again as needed.

If you want to restore those models in the future, you'd need to either:
1. Stream directly from the backup location without staging in `/tmp`
2. Use a bind mount with sufficient space
3. Simply re-pull the models from Ollama's registry

binding the mount with sufficient space for other containerrs will be a big help. openwebui's data wasn't sensitive or even permanent. I will repull the data again next time. but other apps have data that needs to be restored and backed up carefully. so I think we should always check the storage space

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Restore Docker Volumes to LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# Usage: ./restore-docker-volumes.sh <container_id> [backup_dir]
#
# Restores Docker volumes from tar.gz archives to an LXC container.
# Should be run after container recreation.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

VMID="${1:-}"
BACKUP_DIR="${2:-/tank/backups/migration}"
PROXMOX_HOST="${PROXMOX_HOST:-homelab}"

if [[ -z "$VMID" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <container_id> [backup_dir]"
    echo "Example: $0 502 /tank/backups/migration"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== Restoring Docker volumes to LXC $VMID ==="
echo "Backup directory: $BACKUP_DIR"

# Check container is running
if ! ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct status $VMID" | grep -q running; then
    echo "Starting container $VMID..."
    ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct start $VMID"
    sleep 10  # Wait for container to fully boot
fi

# Wait for Docker to be ready
echo "Waiting for Docker daemon..."
for i in {1..30}; do
    if ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker info" &>/dev/null; then
        echo "Docker is ready"
        break
    fi
    sleep 2
done

# Restore /config directory first (contains docker-compose.yml)
CONFIG_BACKUP="${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-config.tar.gz"
if ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "test -f ${CONFIG_BACKUP}"; then
    echo "Restoring /config directory..."
    ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct push $VMID ${CONFIG_BACKUP} /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz"
    ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- tar xzf /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz -C /"
    ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz"
    echo "  -> Restored /config"
else
    echo "No config backup found at ${CONFIG_BACKUP}"
fi

# Get list of volume backups
echo "Looking for volume backups..."
VOLUME_BACKUPS=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "ls ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | grep -v config.tar.gz" || echo "")

if [[ -z "$VOLUME_BACKUPS" ]]; then
    echo "No volume backups found for container $VMID"
else
    for archive in $VOLUME_BACKUPS; do
        # Extract volume name from filename (VMID-volumename.tar.gz)
        filename=$(basename "$archive")
        vol=$(echo "$filename" | sed "s/${VMID}-//" | sed 's/.tar.gz//')

        echo "Restoring volume: $vol"

        # Push archive to container
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct push $VMID ${archive} /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"

        # Create volume if it doesn't exist
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume create $vol" 2>/dev/null || true

        # Restore volume contents using alpine
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
            -v ${vol}:/dest \
            -v /tmp:/backup \
            alpine sh -c 'cd /dest && tar xzf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz'"

        # Clean up temp file
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"

        echo "  -> Restored volume: $vol"
    done
fi

# Start Docker compose stack
echo "Starting Docker services..."
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- bash -c 'cd /config && docker compose up -d'" || true

echo ""
echo "=== Restore complete ==="
echo "Docker containers:"
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker ps"

# Get list of volume backups
echo "Looking for volume backups..."
VOLUME_BACKUPS=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "ls ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | grep -v config.tar.gz" || echo "")

if [[ -z "$VOLUME_BACKUPS" ]]; then
    echo "No volume backups found for container $VMID"
else
    # Check available space in container's /tmp before restoring
    echo "Checking available space in container..."
    AVAILABLE_KB=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- df /tmp 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print \$4}'" || echo "0")
    AVAILABLE_MB=$((AVAILABLE_KB / 1024))
    echo "Available space in /tmp: ${AVAILABLE_MB}MB"

    # Calculate total backup size
    TOTAL_BACKUP_SIZE=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "du -c ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | grep total | awk '{print \$1}'" || echo "0")
    TOTAL_BACKUP_MB=$((TOTAL_BACKUP_SIZE / 1024))
    echo "Total backup size: ${TOTAL_BACKUP_MB}MB"

    # Warn if insufficient space (need at least backup size for staging)
    if [[ $AVAILABLE_KB -lt $TOTAL_BACKUP_SIZE ]]; then
        echo ""
        echo "⚠️  WARNING: Insufficient space in /tmp for restoration!"
        echo "   Available: ${AVAILABLE_MB}MB, Required: ~${TOTAL_BACKUP_MB}MB"
        echo ""
        echo "Options:"
        echo "  1. Increase container rootfs size"
        echo "  2. Mount external storage for staging"
        echo "  3. Restore volumes one at a time (continuing with smaller backups)"
        echo ""
        read -p "Continue with restoration anyway? [y/N] " -n 1 -r
        echo
        if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
            echo "Aborting restoration."
            exit 1
        fi
    fi

    for archive in $VOLUME_BACKUPS; do
        # Extract volume name from filename (VMID-volumename.tar.gz)
        filename=$(basename "$archive")
        vol=$(echo "$filename" | sed "s/${VMID}-//" | sed 's/.tar.gz//')

        # Check individual archive size before restoring
        ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "du -k ${archive} 2>/dev/null | awk '{print \$1}'" || echo "0")
        ARCHIVE_MB=$((ARCHIVE_SIZE / 1024))

        # Re-check available space for each volume
        CURRENT_AVAILABLE=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- df /tmp 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print \$4}'" || echo "0")

        if [[ $CURRENT_AVAILABLE -lt $ARCHIVE_SIZE ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo "⚠️  SKIPPING $vol: Archive size (${ARCHIVE_MB}MB) exceeds available /tmp space ($((CURRENT_AVAILABLE / 1024))MB)"
            echo "   To restore this volume manually:"
            echo "   1. Mount additional storage to container"
            echo "   2. Copy ${archive} to mounted path"
            echo "   3. Extract to Docker volume"
            continue
        fi

        echo "Restoring volume: $vol (${ARCHIVE_MB}MB)"

        # Push archive to container
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct push $VMID ${archive} /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"

        # Create volume if it doesn't exist
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume create $vol" 2>/dev/null || true

        # Restore volume contents using alpine
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
            -v ${vol}:/dest \
            -v /tmp:/backup \
            alpine sh -c 'cd /dest && tar xzf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz'"

        # Clean up temp file
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"

        echo "  -> Restored volume: $vol"
    done
fi

    AVAILABLE_KB=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- df /tmp 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print \$4}'" || echo "0")
    AVAILABLE_MB=$((AVAILABLE_KB / 1024))
    echo "Available space in /tmp: ${AVAILABLE_MB}MB"

    # Calculate total backup size
    TOTAL_BACKUP_SIZE=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "du -c ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | grep total | awk '{print \$1}'" || echo "0")
    TOTAL_BACKUP_MB=$((TOTAL_BACKUP_SIZE / 1024))
    echo "Total backup size: ${TOTAL_BACKUP_MB}MB"

    # Warn if insufficient space (need at least backup size for staging)
    if [[ $AVAILABLE_KB -lt $TOTAL_BACKUP_SIZE ]]; then
        echo ""
        echo "⚠️  WARNING: Insufficient space in /tmp for restoration!"
        echo "   Available: ${AVAILABLE_MB}MB, Required: ~${TOTAL_BACKUP_MB}MB"
        echo ""
        echo "Options:"
        echo "  1. Increase container rootfs size"
        echo "  2. Mount external storage for staging"
        echo "  3. Restore volumes one at a time (continuing with smaller backups)"
        echo ""
        read -p "Continue with restoration anyway? [y/N] " -n 1 -r
        echo
        if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
            echo "Aborting restoration."
            exit 1
        fi
    fi

    for archive in $VOLUME_BACKUPS; do
        # Extract volume name from filename (VMID-volumename.tar.gz)
        filename=$(basename "$archive")
        vol=$(echo "$filename" | sed "s/${VMID}-//" | sed 's/.tar.gz//')

        # Check individual archive size before restoring
        ARCHIVE_SIZE=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "du -k ${archive} 2>/dev/null | awk '{print \$1}'" || echo "0")
        ARCHIVE_MB=$((ARCHIVE_SIZE / 1024))

        # Re-check available space for each volume
        CURRENT_AVAILABLE=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- df /tmp 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print \$4}'" || echo "0")

        if [[ $CURRENT_AVAILABLE -lt $ARCHIVE_SIZE ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo "⚠️  SKIPPING $vol: Archive size (${ARCHIVE_MB}MB) exceeds available /tmp space ($((CURRENT_AVAILABLE / 1024))MB)"
            echo "   To restore this volume manually:"
            echo "   1. Mount additional storage to container"
            echo "   2. Copy ${archive} to mounted path"
            echo "   3. Extract to Docker volume"
            continue
        fi

        echo "Restoring volume: $vol (${ARCHIVE_MB}MB)"

        # Push archive to container
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct push $VMID ${archive} /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"

        # Create volume if it doesn't exist
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume create $vol" 2>/dev/null || true

        # Restore volume contents using alpine
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
            -v ${vol}:/dest \
            -v /tmp:/backup \
            alpine sh -c 'cd /dest && tar xzf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz'"

        # Clean up temp file
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/${vol}.tar.gz"

        echo "  -> Restored volume: $vol"
    done
fi

The diagnostics are just informational notes about shell expansion. In this case, the `awk '{print \$4}'` pattern is intentionally escaped so that `$4` is passed to the remote side (via SSH) and expanded there, not locally. This is correct behavior.

The updated restore script now:

1. **Checks available space upfront** - Shows total backup size vs available `/tmp` space
2. **Warns before proceeding** - If insufficient space, prompts user with options
3. **Checks each volume individually** - Before restoring each archive, verifies space
4. **Skips large volumes gracefully** - Instead of failing mid-restore, it skips volumes that won't fit and provides manual instructions
5. **Shows file sizes** - Displays archive size for each volume being restored

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Backup Docker Volumes from LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# Usage: ./backup-docker-volumes.sh <container_id> [backup_dir]
#
# Exports all Docker volumes from an LXC container to tar.gz archives.
# Stops Docker compose stack to ensure consistent backup.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

VMID="${1:-}"
BACKUP_DIR="${2:-/tank/backups/migration}"
PROXMOX_HOST="${PROXMOX_HOST:-homelab}"

if [[ -z "$VMID" ]]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <container_id> [backup_dir]"
    echo "Example: $0 502 /tank/backups/migration"
    exit 1
fi

echo "=== Backing up Docker volumes from LXC $VMID ==="
echo "Backup directory: $BACKUP_DIR"

# Create backup directory on Proxmox host
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "mkdir -p ${BACKUP_DIR}"

# Stop Docker compose stack for consistent backup
echo "Stopping Docker services..."
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- bash -c 'cd /config && docker compose stop'" || true

# Get list of Docker volumes
echo "Getting list of Docker volumes..."
VOLUMES=$(ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker volume ls -q" || echo "")

if [[ -z "$VOLUMES" ]]; then
    echo "No Docker volumes found in container $VMID"
else
    echo "Found volumes: $VOLUMES"

    # Backup each volume
    for vol in $VOLUMES; do
        echo "Backing up volume: $vol"

        # Create backup inside container using alpine
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- docker run --rm \
            -v ${vol}:/source:ro \
            -v /tmp/backup:/backup \
            alpine tar czf /backup/${vol}.tar.gz -C /source ."

        # Copy backup from container to Proxmox host backup dir
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct pull $VMID /tmp/backup/${vol}.tar.gz ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-${vol}.tar.gz"

        # Clean up temp file in container
        ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/backup/${vol}.tar.gz"

        echo "  -> Saved to ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-${vol}.tar.gz"
    done
fi

# Also backup the /config directory (compose files, app data)
echo "Backing up /config directory..."
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- tar czf /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz -C / config" || true
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct pull $VMID /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-config.tar.gz" || true
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- rm -f /tmp/config-backup.tar.gz" || true

# Restart Docker compose stack
echo "Restarting Docker services..."
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "pct exec $VMID -- bash -c 'cd /config && docker compose up -d'" || true

echo ""
echo "=== Backup complete ==="
echo "Backup files:"
ssh "root@${PROXMOX_HOST}" "ls -lh ${BACKUP_DIR}/${VMID}-*" 2>/dev/null || echo "No backup files found"
